question: For a new customer who says what they feel like eating, does the LLM agent surface the restaurant of their real next order more often than the home page or plain search?
targets: new customers (no order through day 75) in the official DHRD test file; first order of each

llm_sample.note: LLM arms run on a seeded sample to fit the free provider quota; non-LLM arms also run on every new customer

simulated_user: One Portuguese message generated by code from the real order: the vendor's cuisine (fixed template per cuisine) plus 'barato' when the order's priced items are all in the cheapest band. No item or restaurant name is ever used.

arms.home: region x time slot popularity for the order's region and hour (the product home); ignores the message
arms.search_pt: product search box with the cuisine in Portuguese as a person would type it ('comida japonesa'), plus the $ filter when the order was cheap
arms.search_en: product search box with the catalog's own English cuisine word ('japanese'): the best case for lexical search
arms.search_pt_local / search_en_local: the same BM25 top 50, reordered by how often the item's restaurant is ordered in the region and time slot
arms.agent: the product agent (/v1/agent) receiving the full Portuguese message, with the region in its context; items exactly as shown
arms.agent_local: the agent's own search arguments, with the same regional reordering

metrics: restaurant_hit@5: a shown item comes from the restaurant of the real order
item_hit@5: a shown item is in the real order
cuisine_match@5: share of shown items from the cuisine the customer asked for
limitations: Code-generated intents, not people; one turn; the region is known to the home and the agent but plain search has no region input, which is the product as built. Offline replay: measures whether the real choice would have been shown, not satisfaction.
